At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. We're tackling the world's toughest health challenges, building a world where complex diseases are prevented and cured, treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Across Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine and Johnson & Johnson MedTech, our work is grounded in a single purpose: changing health for humanity. Johnson & Johnson is ranked #1 in healthcare across S&P 500 companies in the AIDE Institute's AI adoption index, which assesses how AI is applied in practice across workforce, operations and business outcomes, including work in surgical robotics, digital surgery analytics and imaging systems. At J&J, AI accelerates innovation, improves how we operate, and delivers better outcomes for patients.
The Principal AI Engineer, GenAI Platform Operations is the senior technical authority for how agents run on the enterprise GenAI platform: you set the operations strategy and build the capabilities that observe and control agents in production. That platform includes the MCP (Model Context Protocol) Gateway, the agentic runtime, conversational AI and content-generation services, and Enterprise Knowledge Graph and GraphRAG retrieval services, deployed across Microsoft Azure and AWS and relied upon by scientific, commercial, supply chain and manufacturing teams across our segments. As agents move from pilots into production, keeping the platform available is no longer enough: we need to know what every agent is doing, how well it is performing, and how to intervene while it runs. This is a hands-on technical leadership role: you define that strategy and design and build the control capabilities that deliver it: observability and performance telemetry for agents, a map of agent performance and dependencies across the estate, reliability checks carried out by agents rather than by hand, and a runtime control plane that can throttle, pause, roll back or stop an agent, a tool or a model in seconds, including a tested kill switch. You also own agent lifecycle management at runtime, from registration and promotion through versioning, suspension and retirement, and you lead the platform's support and incident management teams. Because this platform supports regulated and patient-adjacent work, these controls are a quality and safety obligation as much as an engineering one, and you will partner closely with Quality and Compliance and with Information Security & Risk Management (ISRM) so that every control is validated, every control action is traceable, and the platform remains inspection-ready.
You lead the GenAI platform support and incident management teams, and you work with the site reliability, operations and platform engineers, setting the technical standards they operate to and mentoring them through the hardest failure modes. You set the runtime readiness criteria every agent must meet before it is promoted to production, and you turn agent performance signals, including quality regressions, failing tools, unreliable dependencies, runaway cost and unsafe behavior, into prioritized input for the Azure and AWS platform engineering, agentic engineering, model engineering, and AI security and governance teams. Guided by Our Credo, you build an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual, diversity and dignity are respected, merit is recognized, and on-call and escalation work is distributed justly and sustainably.
This position will report into the Senior Manager, TS GenAI platform engineering.
Key Responsibilities:
· Define and own the GenAI platform operations strategy and roadmap — the operating model for running agents in production across Azure and AWS, the observability and control capabilities the platform needs, and the sequence for building them — and publish the agent operations review that turns performance, reliability, risk and cost trends into prioritized platform commitments.
· Build the agent observability platform — end-to-end traces across multi-step agent runs, gateway-mediated MCP tool calls, model calls and retrieval, built on OpenTelemetry and its generative AI semantic conventions — and define the instrumentation contract every agent must implement before it reaches production.
· Monitor agent performance in production: task completion, answer quality and groundedness from online evaluation, tool-call and MCP success rates, latency, token use and cost per task, guardrail interventions, and drift or regression against each version's baseline — with SLOs and error budgets set per agent and per risk tier.
· Map agent performance across the estate: an authoritative agent registry linking each agent to its owner, versions, tools, MCP servers, models, data sources and risk tier; dependency maps that show blast radius; and performance scorecards that let consumers and governance compare agents and act on the weakest.
· Agentify reliability checks: design and deploy operations agents that run health checks, synthetic probes, anomaly triage, evidence gathering and first-line remediation, with defined autonomy limits, human approval for consequential actions and complete audit trails — reducing manual toil and time to detect.
· Build the runtime control plane that influences the platform while it runs — kill switches at agent, tool, MCP server, model and platform level; circuit breakers, rate limits, budget caps, throttling and quarantine; and policy enforcement at the gateway — validated under GxP-compliant change control with Quality and Compliance and ISRM, tested regularly, and with every control action recorded as inspection-ready evidence.
· Own agent lifecycle management at runtime: registration and admission, runtime readiness gates, promotion between environments, versioning, canary and shadow releases, automated rollback on regression, suspension, deprecation and retirement — so no agent runs in production without an owner, a version and an off switch.
· Lead the GenAI platform support team for reliability: L1 and L2 intake, triage runbooks, routing and escalation to L3 engineering, response and resolution commitments, knowledge articles and known-error records — feeding recurring issues back to engineering and documentation, SDK and onboarding gaps to the team that owns the developer-facing surface.
· Lead the incident management team: major incident command, severity classification, bridge coordination, stakeholder communication and restoration, using the runtime control plane to contain agent incidents; and chair blameless reviews and problem management until recurring failure modes are engineered out, with corrective actions owned and closed.
· Lead, hire, coach and develop the support, incident management and reliability engineers in an inclusive, Credo-grounded environment — with an equitable, sustainable on-call rotation — and manage the cloud, observability and agent operations vendors and the managed service provider for L1 support.

· Minimum of 10 years of progressive technology experience, including at least 5 years in enterprise-scale services, and 3 years of formal people leadership managing engineering, operations or support teams.
· Minimum of a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems or a related technical discipline; Master's degree preferred.
· Demonstrated experience defining and technically delivering an operations, reliability or observability strategy and roadmap for a platform serving multiple internal consumer teams.
· Track record of designing and building observability platforms — tracing, metrics, logs, alerting and service health reporting — and using that data to drive engineering prioritization.
· Practical experience operating AI, machine learning or LLM-based services in production, including monitoring their quality and performance, not only their availability.
· Experience building runtime controls for production systems, such as feature flags, circuit breakers, rate limiting, traffic management, emergency stop or automated rollback.
· Hands-on operational experience with workloads running on Microsoft Azure and/or AWS, including containerized services and managed data and networking services.
· Experience operating technology in a regulated environment, with working knowledge of GxP change control, computer system validation, and the evidence expected in internal audits or health authority inspections.
· Experience automating operational work at scale, including health checks, triage and auto-remediation, and reducing toil through engineering.
· Demonstrated accountability for a 24x7 production service, including running ITIL-aligned incident and problem management and an L1/L2 support function for a platform serving multiple internal consumer teams.
· Experience building and leading support, incident management or reliability teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management and creating an inclusive environment where each person is considered as an individual.
· Ability to explain agent behavior, risk and control decisions clearly to senior Technology, business, Quality and governance stakeholders, including when an agent must be paused or stopped.
· Willingness to participate in an escalation rotation supporting a 24x7 platform, including runtime control decisions, and to coordinate across global time zones during major incidents.

· Production evaluation of LLM and agent quality, including online evaluation, LLM-as-judge scoring, groundedness and task-success metrics, and drift and regression detection
· Site reliability engineering practice: SLI and SLO definition, error budget management, capacity planning, failure testing and toil reduction

· Agent lifecycle and release engineering: registries, versioning, canary and shadow releases, promotion gates and retirement
· Building operations agents or AI-assisted automation with defined autonomy limits, human-in-the-loop approval and audit trails
· MCP Gateway and API gateway operations, including policy enforcement, authentication and tool-level access control

· Operational depth in Azure and AWS platform services, including identity, networking, private connectivity, and quota and reserved capacity management

· Production-grade Python or Go for building operational tooling, automation and control services
· GxP change control and validation documentation practice, including traceable approvals and audit evidence for production controls and changes
· People leadership fundamentals: hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, equitable workload and on-call design, and building an inclusive team environment consistent with Our Credo

· Familiarity with Arize, LangSmith and Langfuse

· Chaos engineering and resilience testing, including game days that exercise kill switches and failover
· FinOps for AI workloads, including token and inference cost monitoring, budget enforcement and cost per task

The Principal AI Engineer, GenAI Developer Experience is the senior hands-on engineer who designs and builds the developer-facing surface of our Enterprise GenAI Platform, making it straightforward to adopt for an engineer in Oncology clinical development, a MedTech manufacturing product team, or a Supply Chain engineering team. You will own the technical design and implementation of that surface end to end: the Agent Framework SDKs and client libraries, the MCP Gateway API contracts and versioning policy, the Agent/Skills/MCP catalog that makes capabilities discoverable and reusable, the API Marketplace, self-service onboarding automation, reference architectures and templates, and the docs-as-code that hold it all together. Your work consumes the agentic runtimes built by our cloud-aligned agentic engineering teams on Microsoft Azure and AWS. You do not build the runtime; you design the abstractions that make it usable, discoverable, documented and adoptable by engineering teams across multiple sectors like Innovative Medicine, MedTech and our enterprise functions, within the expectations of a regulated healthcare enterprise.
Success in this role is measured in developer outcomes: how quickly a team moves from idea to a validated agent in production, how often teams reuse a catalogued skill instead of rebuilding it, how seldom they need to raise a support request, and how satisfied they are with the platform. As the technical authority for developer experience, you set the engineering standards for SDK, API and template design, mentor platform and developer-tooling engineers, and work alongside the Manager, GenAI Developer Experience to shape the roadmap - grounded in Our Credo, creating an inclusive environment where each person is considered as an individual, respecting diversity and dignity, recognizing merit, and holding yourself to actions that are just and ethical.
Key Responsibilities:
· Set the technical direction and architecture for the developer-facing surface of the Enterprise GenAI Platform, and shape its roadmap with the Manager, GenAI Developer Experience — making the engineering trade-offs between new capability, hardening and documentation debt explicit across Innovative Medicine, MedTech and enterprise demands.
· Design and own the MCP Gateway's published API contract — OpenAPI specifications, semantic versioning and deprecation policy, backward-compatibility guarantees and contract testing — and engineer the SDK release trains and changelogs consumers depend on.
· Design, build and maintain the Agent Framework SDKs and client libraries in Python and TypeScript so a Johnson & Johnson engineer can register a tool, call the Gateway and stand up an agent against the shared runtime through a small, documented surface.
· Architect and build the Agent, Skills and MCP catalog and the API Marketplace as the enterprise discovery, reuse and entitlement layer — metadata taxonomy, ownership and lifecycle states, certification tiers, search, reuse tracking, consumer registration, self-service quotas and sandbox versus validated environments.
· Engineer the self-service onboarding path from access request to first working agent without manual platform intervention — provisioning, credentials, scaffolding and quickstarts to a documented time target — and build AI capability into the automated deployment pipelines with the Cloud and ISRM teams.
· Author reference architectures, starter templates and golden paths for the patterns teams actually build — retrieval-grounded assistants, tool-using agents, content generation workflows and MCP servers — favoring harness engineering and durable workflow over bespoke agent development, and set the engineering standards for open-source platform development.
· Consume rather than rebuild: design consistent SDK and Gateway abstractions over the Azure and AWS agentic runtimes and feed developer pain points into their roadmaps with reproducible evidence; surface model engineering’s selection guidance, evaluation results and RAG and Knowledge Graph grounding options as documented choices; and align standards with the software engineering developer experience team.
· Make the compliant path the easy path, with AI security and governance and Quality as control owners — engineer guardrail configuration, audit traceability, responsible AI disclosures and ISRM controls into SDK defaults and templates, generate GxP-aware documentation and traceable release records from the pipeline, and integrate emerging compliance frameworks.

Job Description:
This is a duration based role that will last 2 years.
The Principal Data Engineer owns product engineering and architectural decisions, serving as both the technical visionary and hands-on leader responsible for solution delivery. This role partners closely with Product Owners, Product Group Engineers, Lead Engineers, architects, and cross-functional product squads to solve complex engineering challenges, define scalable technical solutions, and ensure alignment with enterprise technology strategy.
The role is accountable for product technical architecture, engineering standards, technology roadmaps, and the successful delivery of scalable, secure, and governed data and AI solutions. The ideal candidate brings 10+ years of progressive experience in enterprise data engineering, architecture, analytics, and AI, with deep expertise in Azure, Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Power BI, Data Mesh, Data Federation, Data Modeling, Data Governance, Enterprise Data Management, Generative AI, and Agentic AI platforms.
Responsibilities:
Lead the end-to-end data integration strategy for the Butterfly program, ensuring seamless data movement across CRM, ERP, MDM, CDP, analytics, and downstream platforms.
Own integration architecture decisions, standards, and patterns across batch, real-time, API-based, event-driven, and file-based integrations.
Partner with business, product, and application teams to define data exchange requirements and align with enterprise data standards.
Drive the design, development, testing, and deployment of scalable integration solutions supporting global releases and country rollouts.
Establish and govern integration design reviews, technical specifications, mapping documents, and interface contracts.
Coordinate cross-functional teams to manage integration dependencies, risks, and release readiness.
Serve as the primary technical lead for application onboarding, source-to-target mapping, integration assessments, and data flow design.
Ensure integration solutions meet performance, reliability, scalability, security, and compliance requirements.
Technical Scope & Expectations (Data Engineering Focus).
Design and implement enterprise integration solutions using APIs, ETL/ELT pipelines, messaging frameworks, event-driven architectures, and cloud-native integration patterns.
Lead source system onboarding and integration of commercial, customer, product, consent, and transactional data into Butterfly data products.
Establish reusable integration frameworks, canonical data models, and standardized mapping approaches to accelerate delivery and reduce complexity.
Embed data quality controls, reconciliation processes, exception handling, and monitoring capabilities into all integration solutions.
Collaborate with MDM, Data Product, Analytics, Experience, and Application teams to support a unified enterprise data ecosystem.
Define integration observability standards, including logging, alerting, monitoring, SLA management, and operational support processes.
Drive API-first integration strategies and support the governance and lifecycle management of enterprise APIs and data services.
Lead migration and modernization efforts from legacy integrations to cloud-native architectures leveraging Azure, Databricks, and Microsoft Fabric.
